# Review: Aeration Control Narrative

**Recommendation:** Do not issue this to the contractor yet. R-01 to R-05 are design errors or gaps that would be built as written. Findings are ordered by severity.

## Findings

| ID | Location | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| R-01 | §2 | **Critical.** "Fixed setpoint" conflicts with "most-open-valve logic resets the setpoint". The two cannot both be true. | Make the PIT-920 setpoint a reset value with a minimum and maximum clamp, a rate limit, and a deadband (SP-AER-005 to 009). Use a fixed setpoint only in manual and as the bad-PV fallback. |
| R-02 | §2 vs §5 | **Critical.** Units differ, and the values contradict. 7.5 psig is about 208 inH2O. The staging thresholds of 160 and 165 inH2O are about 5.8 and 6.0 psig. While PIT-920 holds setpoint, "stage off when above 165" is always true, so blowers would stage off while demand is met. The 5 inH2O band is also too narrow and has no stage-off delay. The thresholds are fixed, but the setpoint moves. | Use one pressure unit (psig). Stage on when PIT-920 is below the *active* setpoint by a set deviation and the running blower output is saturated, for the stage-on delay. Stage off when the remaining blowers can carry the load, for the stage-off delay (SP-AER-010 to 013). |
| R-03 | §3 | **Critical.** Closing the valve on loss of DO starves the basin, which is the opposite of the stated intent. If several valves close, the header dead-heads and the blowers can surge. It also removes the valve from the most-open-valve logic. | On bad AIT-90x: hold the last good valve output, raise an alarm, exclude the basin from the most-open-valve logic, and prompt the operator for manual. Add a blower start permissive and a run-time alarm for minimum open air path (SP-AER-021). |
| R-04 | §6 | **Critical.** "All blowers that were running restart" has no stagger, no outage limit, and no check of coast-down or motor-start limits. Simultaneous starts cause inrush and voltage sag. The restart also runs without checking permissives. | Restart only if the outage is shorter than SP-AER-019. Restart in lead order, one blower per SP-AER-020 interval, and only after all start permissives are true. For a longer outage, prompt the operator. Require operations sign-off on auto-restart. |
| R-05 | §7 | **Critical.** "Blower high vibration trip" has no tag, no trip value, no delay, no start-up inhibit, no latch or reset, and no fail state. It does not say who owns the trip. | Use the vibration alarm and trip values in SP-AER-018 (vendor to confirm). On trip: stop the motor, close the IGV, latch, require a local reset after the cause clears, and start the standby blower. If this is a safety function, reference the SRS. If it is a vendor machinery-protection function, reference that document and still state the BPCS response. |
| R-06 | §4 | Permissive is incomplete. ZSC-931 is one tag for three blowers. The discharge valve has no tag or position switch. | Give per-blower tags (for example ZSC-931/932/933). Add the discharge valve tag and its open switch. Add these permissives: motor starter ready, no lockout, no E-stop, remote mode, lube oil OK, vibration healthy, min-off time elapsed, starts-per-hour not exceeded, minimum open air path. |
| R-07 | General | No ISA-106 state and transition table. Start, run, stop, trip, and restart are undefined. Start has no step timeouts or failure responses. | Add the blower state table (below). Derive step tables with Step, Action, Transition, Timeout, and Failure response. |
| R-08 | §2 | Blower capacity control is undefined. The text does not say what the PIT-920 loop adjusts (IGV, speed, or both), how load is shared, or how surge and blow-off protection work. | State the PV, output, action, mode behavior, and load sharing. State the surge and blow-off response in the blower module. |
| R-09 | §1 | "Air flow control valve" has no flow transmitter. The text does not say whether the DO output is valve position or a flow setpoint. It gives no controller action, output limits, or mode behavior. | State that the output is valve position (or add a FIT and cascade). State reverse action, minimum position (SP-AER-003), and auto/manual behavior with bumpless transfer. |
| R-10 | §1, 2, 5 | Numbers in prose: 2.0 mg/L, 7.5 psig, 85%, 160, 165, 2 min. | Move all values to the setpoint list (below). Refer to them by ID. |
| R-11 | §2 | Most-open-valve logic has gaps. It does not exclude valves in manual, with bad signal, or in out-of-service basins. It has no rate limit and no handling for a valve at 100% when the setpoint is at its maximum. | Exclude those valves. Alarm "insufficient air capacity" when the setpoint is at maximum and the valve is above SP-AER-004 for SP-AER-004A. Add anti-windup. |
| R-12 | §5 | Staging has no lead/lag rotation, minimum run or off times, starts-per-hour limit, or hold-off during a start. It does not say what happens if a started blower fails to start. | Add rotation, SP-AER-014 to 017, a stage hold-off during Starting, and a rule that a fail-to-start commands the next standby blower. |
| R-13 | General | Abnormal handling is missing. Bad PIT-920, comms loss, PLC restart, and fail positions of FCV-911 to 914, IGVs, and discharge valves are undefined. | Bad PIT-920: hold blower output and setpoint, freeze staging, alarm. Comms loss: blowers continue on last setpoint, with local control available. Specify each fail position. A fail-open or fail-as-is valve is preferred (see R-03). |
| R-14 | General | No cause-and-effect chart or alarm list. | Write the interlock rows here if no chart exists. Alarms needed: DO bad PV, DO low and high, valve high position, header pressure low and high, insufficient air capacity, blower fail to start, blower trip, vibration high, auto-restart active. Give each a response. |
| R-15 | General | No requirement IDs, test methods, purpose and boundaries, operator interface, automation levels, or open items. | Apply the module template. Use FR-AER-NNN IDs, each with a FAT test. Require operations sign-off on states and prompts. Do the STE pass last. |

## Minimum blower state table (ISA-106)

| State | Entry condition | Allowed exits | Initiator | Automation level |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stopped, not ready | Any start permissive false | Stopped, ready | Auto | Automatic |
| Stopped, ready | All permissives true | Starting | Staging, operator, or restart sequence | Automatic or operator-prompted |
| Starting | Start command | Running; Tripped (timeout or fault) | Auto | Automatic |
| Running | Motor running, run-up complete | Stopping; Tripped | Staging or operator | Automatic |
| Stopping | Stop command | Stopped, not ready; Tripped (timeout) | Staging or operator | Automatic |
| Tripped (latched) | Any trip | Stopped, not ready, after local reset | Operator | Manual |
